Georgia's broad-based categorical eligibility (SNAP state option;
PolicyEngine models gross screen x1.3 FPL, x2.0 for elderly/disabled
households, at 2026-01 per gov/hhs/tanf/non_cash parameters) is not in
the composed us-ga/snap/fy-2026 program, which applies only the standard
federal tests. Every selected row is verified per-row against axiom's
persisted output surface: household gross income sits inside the band
above the federal 130 percent limit the composed program applies and at
or below the state's BBCE screen, verified against axiom's own computed
gross income and limit. Axiom-side modeling boundary, tracked for
encoding in rulespec-us#1098.

Exact-household requested-month counterfactual on PolicyEngine 4.18.9 / PolicyEngine-US 1.767.3 / PolicyEngine-Core 3.30.3. The committed comparison adapter replayed over the same Case projection reproduces the report pin (Axiom 1467.0 versus January PolicyEngine 1432.699951171875), and the unmodified direct requested-month simulation reproduces the same January value. Forcing the aggregate and state TANF inputs to zero in the direct requested-month simulation produces January SNAP 1467.5; its absolute delta from Axiom, 0.5, is within the unchanged suite tolerance 7.0. The comparison bridge zeroes TANF on the Axiom input surface while PolicyEngine computes state TANF endogenously and counts it as SNAP unearned income (axiom-oracles#397 counterfactual class). Replay classifier record: class=tanf.

Exact-household requested-month replay on PolicyEngine 4.18.9 / PolicyEngine-US 1.767.3 / PolicyEngine-Core 3.30.3. The committed PolicyEngine value for this row reproduces bit-exact only through the comparison runner's single-case fallback path (PolicyEngineRunner.run_case -> policyengine household calculator: January SNAP 62.49998474121094 vs report pin 62.49998474121094); the batch dataset path — the suite's primary evaluation path, fed the identical Case inputs — returns a different January value, so the committed row reflects harness path divergence rather than an engine rule difference. The divergence is the fallback path's endogenous SSI imputation, absent from the batch input surface and from the Axiom projection: re-running the same fallback path with the SSI input forced to zero produces January SNAP 298.0, whose absolute delta from Axiom, 0.0, is within the unchanged suite tolerance 7.0. The engines priced different income surfaces (axiom-oracles#397 endogenous-income counterfactual family; a dedicated issue for the SSI imputation and for the batch-vs-fallback path inconsistency still needs filing).

Disability-surface projection asymmetry, the SNAP analogue of the ssi-ecps disposition (axiom-oracles#228): the populace projection maps the Enhanced CPS is_disabled flag into Axiom's snap_member_is_elderly_or_disabled input (elderly_or_disabled transform in axiom_oracles/data/populace_input_mapping.yaml), while PolicyEngine's SNAP elderly/disabled status (has_usda_elderly_disabled) requires receipt of a disability program, which the projected input surface zeroes.
